baslik: Why the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Tore Itself Apart

sahneler.metin: This is the most famous engineering failure ever caught on film.
Nineteen forty. The brand new Tacoma Narrows Bridge.
A forty mile an hour wind, and the entire deck begins to twist.
This is not slow motion. The road is corkscrewing in real time.
One man escapes on his hands and knees.
Then the center span lets go, and drops into the water below.
The bridge was feeding the winds own energy back into its motion.
That is why every big bridge today is tested in a wind tunnel.

aciklama:
In 1940, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge twisted itself apart in a 40 mph wind — the most famous engineering failure ever caught on film. This is why it happened.
